forgot.title: Reset your password

forgot.sent: If that address has an account, a link is on its way. It works for one hour.

conflict.message: Someone else just changed this to “{{value}}”.

my_fields.title: My fields
my_fields.help: Numbers you track for yourself. Colleagues can see them next to your name, and only you can change them.

help.institution: Who you are and how the tool counts years. The defaults work, so change only what differs.
help.users: Invite people and choose what they can do. People are switched off rather than deleted, so their name stays in the history.
help.lists: The values people choose from. To retire an entry, switch off Active: releases that use it keep it.
help.researchers: Everyone named on a release. Tidy up names, add identifiers, merge duplicates and split records that cover two people. Nothing here changes any statistics, because releases refer to the record and not the name.
help.form: Adapt the fields on a release: rename, hide, require or reorder them, or add your own.
help.checkpoints: The moments around a release when numbers are collected, and which numbers those are.
help.data: Your backups, a full copy of your data, and what the automatic jobs have been doing.
help.integrations: Connections to outside services. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.

institution.timezone_hint: Dates show in this time zone. Nightly jobs switch over at the next restart.
institution.website_domain_hint: Website views count only for releases on exactly this address, for example news.example.org.
institution.contact_email_hint: Sent to Crossref when looking up papers. Use a shared office address, not a person's.
institution.code_pattern_hint: Release Radar assigns the codes itself. {yyyy} is the academic year and {nn} the number. A change affects new codes only: existing codes never change.
institution.landing_hint: The first page after signing in. Someone with no writer entry always lands on all releases.

users.name: Name
users.no_email: The email couldn't be sent. Please pass this temporary password on to {{email}} yourself:
users.new_password_question: Sign them out and send a new one?
users.reset_sent: A new temporary password was emailed to {{email}}.
users.personal_help: Fields people track for themselves. When someone leaves, pass theirs on or make them institution fields. The values stay either way.
users.personal_convert_question: Everyone will use this field from now on. Continue?

lists.writers_help: Writers need no account, so former staff can stay on their releases.
lists.vocabularies_help: Named lists of choices for custom fields, in both languages.
lists.release_types_help: What kind of release it is, after EurekAlert's categories. Analysis will keep the types apart, so each release should have the right one.
lists.default_release_type_hint: Imported releases too. Anyone can change a release's type afterwards.

form.core_help: Leave a label empty to keep the standard one. Hidden fields keep their data.
form.cannot_hide: Release Radar relies on this field, so it stays visible.
form.custom_help: Extra fields for everyone in your institution. Personal ones are under My fields in the account menu.

checkpoints.measures_help: The numbers collected at each checkpoint. Switching one off keeps what was recorded.
checkpoints.locked: Goes live with pickups, in a later phase.
checkpoints.reminders_later: The choice above is saved already. The reminder emails themselves arrive in a later phase.
checkpoints.offset_help: A negative number falls before the release date: −3 is three days before. Reminders go out at the start of the day you choose.

ga4.title: Google Analytics
ga4.help: Website views come from Google Analytics: each release's page on {{domain}}, counted over its first 28 days. Every day after the nightly backup, Release Radar fetches the releases whose 28 days and 2 days' processing have passed.
ga4.help_no_domain: Website views come from Google Analytics. Set your news website in Settings → Institution first: only releases on it have website views.
ga4.manual: How to connect it, step by step
ga4.key_unreadable: The stored key cannot be read on this install; enter it again.
ga4.key_hint: The file Google Cloud downloaded. It is stored encrypted and never shown again. Afterwards, keep it in the password manager and delete the downloaded copy.
ga4.property_hint: Digits only: Google Analytics → Admin → Property details.
ga4.fetch_started: Fetching website views. This page shows the result when it's done.
ga4.remove_question: Remove the key? Website views already fetched stay.

test.connected: Connected. Google Analytics counted {{views}} page views on {{host}} on {{date}}.
test.connected_any_host: Connected. Google Analytics counted {{views}} page views on {{date}}.
test.connected_no_views: Connected, but Google Analytics counted no page views on {{host}} on {{date}}. Check that this property is the one for {{host}}.
test.key_rejected: Google refused the key. It may have been deleted or disabled in Google Cloud: create a new key and choose it here.
test.api_disabled: The Google Analytics Data API is not enabled in this key's Google Cloud project. Enable it under APIs & Services → Library, then test again.
test.no_access: The service account has no access to this property. In Google Analytics → Admin → Property access management, add its address as Viewer, and check the property ID.
test.wrong_property: Google Analytics does not accept this property ID. It is digits only, under Admin → Property details.
test.quota: Google Analytics' quota for this property is used up for now. Try again in an hour.
test.unreachable: Google could not be reached. Check the internet connection of the computer Release Radar runs on.
test.google_error: Google Analytics answered with an error.

ga4.schedule_daily: Every day, after the nightly backup. First fetched {{when}}.
ga4.schedule_waiting: Daily fetches start after the first Fetch now. The first one fetches every release since the new website went live.
ga4.counts_text: {{fetched}} with website views from Google Analytics, {{waiting}} still waiting, {{open}} within their 28 days.
ga4.waiting_help: Their 28 days and 2 days' processing have passed, yet they have no website views. After a fetch, this means Google Analytics has no data for the page's address: check it in the record. A number entered by hand in the record always counts instead.
ga4.waiting_help_before: Their 28 days and 2 days' processing have passed. Fetch now fetches them.

data.backup_not_configured: Backups are off, because no passphrase is set on the server. Please ask whoever runs the server.
data.export_help: A complete copy of your data for safekeeping. Passwords and sessions are left out.

import.help: Brings in the releases from the press-release workbook (sheet PR DATA), with the staff, units, fields and two-name releases from the intake workbook. Check first: a check changes nothing and lists everything worth a look. Importing again later finds each release by its code, updates it, and never empties anything.
import.owners: Whose are the personal fields in the workbook?
import.owners_help: Each becomes that person's own field, with the workbook's values. Leave one as it is to skip it; importing again later adds it.
import.takes_time: Each DOI is looked up at Crossref: about half a minute.
import.dry_run: What an import would do (nothing has changed yet)
import.levels: To check: {{check}} · dashes and N/A: {{dash}} · changed on reading: {{info}}
import.before_import: Please read the report first. Import does exactly what was checked, in one go.
import.check_again: The files or owners changed since the check: check again first.

researchers.name: Name as entered
researchers.merge_hint: Search for the record to keep. Its details stay, and gaps are filled from this one. You can undo this later, under Split.
researchers.notes_hint: Anything that tells namesakes apart, such as a lab or a topic.
researchers.split_title: Move releases from {{name}} to another record
researchers.split_hint: For when one record covers two people. Tick the releases that belong to the other person.
researchers.split_none: This record has no releases to move.

custom_field.options_hint: One per line, with the Japanese after a bar: Newspaper | 新聞
custom_field.due_hint: Shows up as a reminder at this checkpoint.

data.columns_not_saved: Your column choice couldn't be saved. It applies until you leave this page.
data.keys_hint: Type to edit, Enter to save and go down, Esc to go back, double-click or Shift+Enter for the full record, Cmd/Ctrl+Z to undo.
data.open_hint: Double-click a release, or press Shift+Enter, for the full record.
data.empty: No releases here yet. Paste a DOI or type a title above.
data.empty_no_writer: Nothing is yours yet, as you have no writer entry. An admin can link one under Settings → Lists → Writers.
data.code_hint: Assigned when a release date is first entered.
data.caught_up: All caught up. Nothing is due.
data.failed_hint: Press Enter or Backspace to correct it, or Esc to go back to what was there.
data.paste_result: {{saved}} saved, {{invalid}} invalid: see the highlighted cells.
data.undo_failed: That couldn't be undone. Someone may have changed it since.
data.crossref_not_found: Crossref doesn't know this DOI. The release is saved, and the paper details can be typed in.
data.crossref_unavailable: Crossref can't be reached just now. The release is saved. You can fetch the paper details later from the release.
data.refetch_question: Replace the journal, paper title, date and authors with Crossref's?

warnings.website_off_domain: This isn't on your news website, so website views won't apply. It's saved anyway.

data.not_a_number: Please enter a number, or - if it doesn't apply.
data.sort_hint: Sort by {{column}}. Click again to reverse, and a third time for newest first.

export.xlsx: Excel, with the lists and a Read me sheet
export.personal_data: The file contains personal data, such as researchers' names. Keep it within the office and delete copies you no longer need.

data.open_link: Open the {{field}} in a new tab

writers.caption: Releases per writer and month in {{year}}, counted by release date. Click a name to see those releases on the Data page.
writers.caption_all: Releases per writer and academic year, counted by release date. Click a name to see those releases on the Data page.
writers.inactive: No longer active in the writers list
writers.undated: Not counted yet: releases without a release date ({{count}}).
writers.export_xlsx: Excel, with a Read me sheet
writers.export_notice: The file contains colleagues' names. Keep it within the office.
